import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# First Hardy–Littlewood conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Hardy%E2%80%93Littlewood_conjecture)
-/

open Filter

open scoped Nat.Prime

/-  ## First Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture -/

namespace HardyLittlewood

/--
A prime constellation is a tuple $(p, p + m_1, \dots, p + m_k)$ such that the $m_i$ are
all positive even integers and every entry is a prime number.
-/
def IsPrimeConstellation {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ) (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  m 0 = 0 ∧ (∀ i ≠ 0, 0 < m i) ∧ (∀ i, p + 2 * m i |>.Prime)

/--
A prime constellation is said to be admissible if its elements do not form a complete
set of residue classes with respect to any prime.
-/
def IsAdmissiblePrimeConstellation {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ) (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsPrimeConstellation m p ∧ ∀ (q : ℕ), q.Prime → ¬(fun i => (p + 2 * m i : ZMod q)).Surjective

/--
The number of distinct residue classes amongst a tuple $(m_0, \dots, m_k)$ for a prime $q$.
-/
noncomputable def Nat.numResidues (q : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Set.range (fun i => (m i : ZMod q)) |>.ncard

/--
For a given tuple $(m_1, \dots, m_k)$, this counts number of admissible
prime constellations $(p, p + m_1, \dots, p + m_k)$ where $p \leq n$.
-/
noncomputable def Nat.primeTupleCounting {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  open scoped Classical in
  Nat.count (IsAdmissiblePrimeConstellation m) n.succ

def FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  let C : ℝ :=
      2 ^ k * ∏' (q : { q : ℕ // q.Prime ∧ 3 ≤ q}),
        (1 - (Nat.numResidues q m : ℝ) / q) / (1 - 1 / q) ^ k.succ
    let π_P : ℕ → ℝ := fun n => (Nat.primeTupleCounting m n : ℝ)
    π_P =O[atTop] fun n => C * ∫ t in (2)..n, 1 / t.log ^ k.succ

/--
Let $P = (m_1, \dots, m_k)$ be a tuple of positive even integers. Let
$\pi_P(n)$ denote the number of primes $p\leq n$ such that $(p, p + m_1, \dots, p + m_k)$
forms an admissible prime constellation. Let $w(q; m_1, \dots, m_k)$ denote the
number of distinct residues of $0, m_1, \dots, m_k$ modulo $q$, and let
$$
  C_P = 2 ^ k\prod_{\substack{q\ \text{prime} \\ q\geq 3}}
    \frac{1 - \frac{w(q; m_1, \dots, m_k)}{q}}{\left(1 - \frac{1}{q}\right)^{k+1}}.
$$
Then
$$
  \pi_P(n)\sim C_P\int_2^n\frac{dt}{\log^{k+1}t}.
$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem first_hardy_littlewood_conjecture {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ) :
    FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor m := by
  sorry

-- Wikipedia URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Hardy%E2%80%93Littlewood_conjecture
/-  ## Second Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture -/
def SecondHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor (x y : ℕ) : Prop :=
  π (x + y) ≤ π x + π y

/--
For integers $x, y \geq 2$,
$$
  \pi(x + y) \leq \pi(x) + \pi(y),
$$
where $\pi(z)$ denotes the prime-counting function, giving the number of primes up to
and including $z$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem second_hardy_littlewood_conjecture {x y : ℕ} (hx : 2 ≤ x) (hy : 2 ≤ y) :
    SecondHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor x y := by
  sorry

/-- Richards [Ri74] showed that only one of the two Hardy-Littlewood conjectures can be true.

[Ri74] Richards, Ian (1974). _On the Incompatibility of Two Conjectures Concerning Primes_. Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 80: 419–438.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem not_first_and_secondHardyLittlewoodConjecture :
    (∀ {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ), FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor m) →
      ¬(∀ {x y : ℕ} (hx : 2 ≤ x) (hy : 2 ≤ y), SecondHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor x y) := by
  sorry

end HardyLittlewood

findings.description: Line 66 uses `π_P =O[atTop] ...`, whereas the source asserts asymptotic equivalence. This only requires an eventual upper bound with an unspecified multiplicative constant. Even for a legitimate distinct admissible pattern, the positive singular-series constant C is absorbed completely into the implicit big-O constant; neither the predicted leading coefficient nor any lower bound or infinitude is asserted. The scratch checks verify that multiplication by a nonzero C does not change a big-O statement and that the zero function satisfies such an upper bound. This misdefined predicate is also used by `first_hardy_littlewood_conjecture` and in the premise of the Richards incompatibility theorem.
findings.source_evidence: The cited Wikipedia article, “First Hardy–Littlewood conjecture,” Statement section, explicitly gives `π_P(n) ∼ C_P ∫₂ⁿ dt/log^{k+1}(t)`: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Hardy%E2%80%93Littlewood_conjecture. Tóth, arXiv:1910.02636, §1, Conjecture 1, repeats this formula and explains that it immediately implies infinitude. Richards (1974), §§1.9–1.10, obtains incompatibility from existence/infinitude of admissible prime tuples, not an upper bound.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `Asymptotics.IsEquivalent`, written `π_P ~[atTop] (fun n => C * ∫ t in (2)..n, 1 / t.log ^ k.succ)` after opening the Asymptotics scope. Put this assertion under appropriate normalized, distinct, admissible-pattern conditions, as described in the other finding; merely changing the relation would make the currently unrestricted malformed-pattern cases problematic.

findings.description: The theorem quantifies over every `m : Fin k.succ → ℕ`, and neither it nor `IsPrimeConstellation` requires distinct offsets. For `k = 2`, `m = ![0,1,1]` is accepted: at p = 3 it represents (3,5,5), and its entire counting function equals the ordinary twin-prime counting function for `![0,1]`. Nevertheless, the formula uses logarithmic exponent 3. There is also a reachable infinite-product default: for every odd prime q the factor is `(1-2/q)/(1-1/q)^3 ≥ 1+1/(4q)`, so the product is not multipliable. Mathlib therefore assigns `tprod = 1`, making C = 4. In `witnesses.lean`, `ReviewCombined.repeated_instance` proves that this literal instance is precisely the twin-prime count being `O(4 * ∫₂ⁿ dt/log³(t))`. This is incompatible with the source's twin-prime prediction, proportional to the log² integral, since the ratio of those integrals grows like log n.
findings.source_evidence: Richards (1974), §1.5, p. 423, defines an admissible tuple as “a k-tuple of distinct integers b₁, …, bₖ.” The linked prime-k-tuple article likewise specifies distinct positive even offsets: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_k-tuple. Tóth, arXiv:1910.02636, §1, introduces increasing positive even offsets. The cited first-conjecture page explicitly gives logarithmic exponent 2 for twin primes.
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude repetitions from the patterns to which the conjecture applies. For example, guard `FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor m` by `m 0 = 0 ∧ Function.Injective m ∧ ∀ q : ℕ, q.Prime → ¬Function.Surjective (fun i => (2 * m i : ZMod q))`. Normalization and injectivity over ℕ imply positivity of every other half-offset. Reflect distinctness in `IsPrimeConstellation` as well, and ensure both the first theorem and Richards's premise use the guarded conjecture. The admissibility guard should concern offsets alone, not assume an existing prime occurrence. Alternatively, deduplicate the offsets and use their actual cardinality throughout the formula.

reformulations.difference: The implementation represents actual even offsets by `2 * m i`, allowing natural-number half-offsets, and includes the zeroth offset explicitly.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every positive even offset a has a unique representation a = 2m with m > 0, and conversely. The condition m 0 = 0 supplies the initial prime p. Doubling also preserves distinctness when that missing condition is imposed. `Review.half_offset_equivalence` proves the exact equivalence between the doubled-offset predicate and a direct positive-even-offset predicate. This parametrization is harmless; it does not excuse the separately reported repetition issue.

reformulations.difference: The Euler product counts residues of the half-offsets m i, although the prime occurrences use p + 2*m i.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every prime q ≥ 3, the map z ↦ p + 2z is a bijection of ZMod q. Thus the ranges of m i and p + 2*m i have equal cardinalities, proved in `Review.affine_residueCount`. Translation-invariance of the admissibility condition is also proved. The excluded prime 2 contributes exactly `(1-1/2)/(1-1/2)^(k+1) = 2^k`, already present in C. There is no missing factor of two or incorrect residue count here.

reformulations.difference: The implementation counts p ≤ n, while the first-conjecture source defines its count using p < n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The counts differ by the indicator of whether n itself is an admissible prime occurrence, hence by at most one. For each intended distinct admissible pattern, C is positive and the logarithmic integral tends to infinity, so this difference is little-o of the main term. The asymptotic formulations are therefore equivalent. Lean proves the exact endpoint identity and the general asymptotic ↔ for any growing main term in `Review.cutoff_equivalence`; the positivity/growth specialization to the full singular-series integral was justified mathematically rather than proved in Lean.

Added injectivity to IsPrimeConstellation and updated affected docstrings to clarify half-offsets. Richards’s premise now uses the corrected predicate automatically. The required compile succeeds with only the existing sorry warnings; additional checks confirm valid singleton/twin patterns and exclusion of repeated offsets.

/-!

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Hardy%E2%80%93Littlewood_conjecture)

open Filter

open scoped Nat.Prime Asymptotics

namespace HardyLittlewood

/--
A prime constellation is a tuple $(p, p + 2m_1, \dots, p + 2m_k)$ with distinct
positive even offsets $2m_i$ and every entry prime. We include the initial offset
by requiring $m_0 = 0$.
-/
def IsPrimeConstellation {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ) (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  m 0 = 0 ∧ Function.Injective m ∧ (∀ i ≠ 0, 0 < m i) ∧ (∀ i, p + 2 * m i |>.Prime)

/--
A prime constellation is said to be admissible if its elements do not form a complete
set of residue classes with respect to any prime.
-/
def IsAdmissiblePrimeConstellation {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ) (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsPrimeConstellation m p ∧ ∀ (q : ℕ), q.Prime → ¬(fun i => (p + 2 * m i : ZMod q)).Surjective

/--
The number of distinct residue classes amongst a tuple $(m_0, \dots, m_k)$ for a prime $q$.
-/
noncomputable def Nat.numResidues (q : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Set.range (fun i => (m i : ZMod q)) |>.ncard

/--
For a given tuple of half-offsets $(m_0, \dots, m_k)$, this counts admissible
prime constellations $(p, p + 2m_1, \dots, p + 2m_k)$ where $p \leq n$.
-/
noncomputable def Nat.primeTupleCounting {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  open scoped Classical in
  Nat.count (IsAdmissiblePrimeConstellation m) n.succ

/-- The first Hardy–Littlewood conjecture for a normalized, distinct, admissible
pattern of even offsets $2m_i$. -/
def FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  (m 0 = 0 ∧ Function.Injective m ∧
    ∀ q : ℕ, q.Prime → ¬(fun i => (2 * m i : ZMod q)).Surjective) →
    let C : ℝ :=
      2 ^ k * ∏' (q : { q : ℕ // q.Prime ∧ 3 ≤ q}),
        (1 - (Nat.numResidues q m : ℝ) / q) / (1 - 1 / q) ^ k.succ
    let π_P : ℕ → ℝ := fun n => (Nat.primeTupleCounting m n : ℝ)
    π_P ~[atTop] fun n => C * ∫ t in (2)..n, 1 / t.log ^ k.succ

/--
Let $m_0 = 0$ and let $m_1, \dots, m_k$ be distinct positive integers. Suppose that
$P = (0, 2m_1, \dots, 2m_k)$ omits a residue class modulo every prime. Let
$\pi_P(n)$ denote the number of primes $p\leq n$ such that $(p, p + 2m_1, \dots, p + 2m_k)$
forms an admissible prime constellation. Let $w(q; m_1, \dots, m_k)$ denote the
number of distinct residues of $0, m_1, \dots, m_k$ modulo $q$. For odd primes $q$,
this is also the number of distinct residues of $P$. Set
$$
  C_P = 2 ^ k\prod_{\substack{q\ \text{prime} \\ q\geq 3}}
    \frac{1 - \frac{w(q; m_1, \dots, m_k)}{q}}{\left(1 - \frac{1}{q}\right)^{k+1}}.
$$
Then
$$
  \pi_P(n)\sim C_P\int_2^n\frac{dt}{\log^{k+1}t}.
$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem first_hardy_littlewood_conjecture {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ) :
    FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor m := by
  sorry

-- Wikipedia URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Hardy%E2%80%93Littlewood_conjecture
/-  ## Second Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture -/
def SecondHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor (x y : ℕ) : Prop :=
  π (x + y) ≤ π x + π y

/--
For integers $x, y \geq 2$,
$$
  \pi(x + y) \leq \pi(x) + \pi(y),
$$
where $\pi(z)$ denotes the prime-counting function, giving the number of primes up to
and including $z$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem second_hardy_littlewood_conjecture {x y : ℕ} (hx : 2 ≤ x) (hy : 2 ≤ y) :
    SecondHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor x y := by
  sorry

/-- Richards [Ri74] showed that only one of the two Hardy-Littlewood conjectures can be true.

[Ri74] Richards, Ian (1974). _On the Incompatibility of Two Conjectures Concerning Primes_. Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 80: 419–438.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem not_first_and_secondHardyLittlewoodConjecture :
    (∀ {k : ℕ} (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ), FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor m) →
      ¬(∀ {x y : ℕ} (hx : 2 ≤ x) (hy : 2 ≤ y), SecondHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor x y) := by
  sorry

end HardyLittlewood
